original_method: Map system sockets and DF IOM instances; prove errortype0 source semantics; decode threshold involvement; read and document S5_RESET_STATUS access/clear behavior before injection; capture durable logs and OOB console; inject one socket once; timestamp SyncFlood/reset/firmware/boot; correlate fresh BERT/CPER IOM source and reset-cause transition; verify DF-attached I/O; clear/restore status and all BIOS/HDT state.
manual_activity: The FAE maps DF IOM per socket, approves errortype and reset policy, handles HDT register pre-state/clear/readback, runs one watchdog injection under OOB console and restores platform state.

MCA threshold FF5/FFE encoding, relevance and raw before/target/restore values

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run one mapped IOM watchdog fault with raw reset-cause pre/post evidence and durable source-specific BERT correlation, then prove all fabric I/O recovered.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds per-socket coverage, sticky-bit hygiene, IOM/CCM discrimination, durable timing, threshold rollback and DF dependency health.

modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The injected watchdog can reset the host, interrupt multiple I/O paths, fail to reboot or leave ambiguous persistent reset status.

project_override_considerations: If S5_RESET_STATUS is sticky across boots, acceptance requires a documented pre-state and approved clear/readback cycle; never erase existing forensic evidence merely to force zero. Multi-socket systems need explicit coverage rather than implicit socket0 sufficiency.

Tool/spec flag mapping plus raw threshold and reset-status pre-state
One complete injection transcript with OOB SyncFlood/reset/firmware/boot timeline
Fresh decoded IOM-specific BERT/CPER record and S5 SyncFlood transition
Recovered OS and all DF-attached devices/services with no persistent watchdog state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Socket0 and errortype0 lack topology/vendor authority; threshold FF5/FFE relevance is unexplained. SyncFlood=1 has no pre-state, clear or freshness rule, so a sticky bit can falsely pass. Exact IOM-specific BERT fields, cross-OS method, reset/boot timeout and RDIMM relevance are missing; DeepSeek's live grep cannot bridge reset.

blocked_analysis.analysis: DF IOM WDT reset intent is clear. Engineering can supply source mapping, register semantics and durable oracle, so static review completes while execution remains gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 74 Wistron-System RAS-00794-V002: map DF IOM per socket and prove --dferror errortype=0 semantics; define FF5/FFE threshold relevance/raw values; provide S5_RESET_STATUS[SyncFlood] persistence and approved pre-state/clear/freshness method; specify IOM-specific fresh BERT/CPER fields, supported OS, reset/firmware/boot/OS deadlines, DF-I/O recovery, aborts, OOB recovery, RDIMM relevance and restoration.

review_improvement: Adds source-specific IOM discrimination and a defensible fresh SyncFlood reset-cause transition, preventing stale sticky status and generic watchdog text from passing the case.
independent_technical_reasoning: A watchdog reset can produce similar high-level symptoms for different DF blocks, so errortype/source decoding and persistent CPER fields are needed to distinguish IOM from CCM. Reset-cause registers are often sticky; reading one after boot without pre-state/clear semantics cannot attribute the bit to this run. Because DF IOM serves multiple data paths, recovery must include downstream I/O health, not only OS boot.
